text:
A: Hi, can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, loud and clear. Gareth.
A: Jasmine. Hi.
B: Nice cat, by the way. I saw it in the photo. Half a cat, anyway.
A: Oh, Biscuit, yeah. She's somewhere knocking things off the counter, probably. Where are you?
B: Walthamstow. North-east London. You?
A: Plymouth.
B: Long way off. What d'you do down there?
A: I own two bubble tea shops in the city centre. Franchise ones. I'm the director, so I do the rotas, the stock orders, the books, talk to the suppliers. I've got a supervisor full-time for the day-to-day, so I only do about twelve hours a week, which is how I like it, to be fair.
B: Twelve hours. That's a sort of dream setup, isn't it.
A: Took a lot to get there. First one was 2019, then the second in 2022. What about you?
B: Structural engineer. Consultancy in Farringdon. Mostly residential conversions, some commercial refurbs. Basically working out whether your loft conversion's going to fall through the ceiling.
A: And does it?
B: Not if I've done it. Er, the architects try their best though. I've just had to redo a whole set of calcs because one of them moved a wall. Didn't tell anyone.
A: That's annoying.
B: Yeah, a bit.
A: Do you own your place, then? Since you know about buildings.
B: Nah. Renting. One-bed in a Victorian conversion. Landlord's been promising to fix the bathroom extractor fan for two years.
A: Two years? You should hold back the rent, honestly.
B: Probably should. Can't be bothered with the fight, really.
A: I would. I read every clause in my leases. Landlords will try it on if you let them.
B: You sound like you enjoy that bit.
A: Bit, yeah. I like a good haggle. Suppliers as well. Erm, we rent too, me and my partner, but I'm always on Rightmove. I want a couple of buy-to-lets eventually.
B: London numbers just annoy me. I look and then I close the app.
A: Plymouth's much better, to be fair. You'd get a whole house for your one-bed.
B: Yeah, and then I'd live in Plymouth.
A: Hey. It's nice. The Hoe, Wembury, the sea.
B: Fair enough, I've never been. Do you actually drink the bubble tea?
A: Not that much anymore. When you do the stock count every week you go off it, lah. Brown sugar one is still good though.
B: I've never had one. The balls put me off, sort of a texture thing.
A: Everyone says that. Then they try it and they come back every week.
B: That's the business model, is it?
A: Basically, yeah. I want a third one, maybe in Exeter. Without working more hours.
B: Good luck with that. I'd like fewer hours and no timesheets. Thought about going freelance.
A: Why don't you?
B: Er, haven't got round to it. Bit of a pattern, to be honest.
A: You just register a company, it's not hard. Takes like twenty minutes on Companies House.
B: It's the bit after the twenty minutes I'm worried about.
A: Clients, yeah. That's the actual work.
B: Exactly. And I'm told I'm a bit blunt with clients.
A: Blunt's fine. I'm blunt with my staff. They still turn up.
B: Mostly, yeah?
A: Except Saturdays. Someone always calls in sick on a Saturday, I swear. It's—
